text:
Sandis Vilmanis was drafted 157th overall in 2022, and on Wednesday night he was the best player on the ice, scoring twice and adding two assists in FLA's 5-3 win over CHI. The Blackhawks are now winless in four (0-3-1), and this one got away early. Vilmanis opened the scoring at 4:43 of the first, Carter Verhaeghe made it 2-0 on the power play, and Seth Jones stretched the lead to 3-0 in the second.

The numbers say Florida earned it. Our model puts the Panthers' expected goals (a measure of the quality of chances) at 4.06 to Chicago's 2.23, and in the share of simulated replays of every shot they win, FLA comes out ahead 68 percent of the time. They outshot the Blackhawks 30-20, outhit them 28-12 and owned the second period, 1.39 to 0.82 in expected goals. The best chance that didn't go in was Sam Reinhart's 32 percent look in the second, stopped by Spencer Knight.

Chicago made it uncomfortable anyway. Roman Kantserov scored late in the second, and Frank Nazar tied up the third with a short-handed backhand before adding a 3 percent chance in the third, cutting it to 4-3 with Connor Bedard assisting. Vilmanis had pushed the lead to 4-2 between those goals, and Reinhart sealed it at 18:33. FLA took the season series 2-0 after a 3-2 win on Oct. 25, while Chicago heads into its next game still looking for a first win in four.
